_meta.how_to_regress: npm run check:golden drive-home  (dev backend up)
_meta.note: V2 rewrite, 2026-08-25. Replaces the v1 sample outright: the old tool ran web_search and spoke confidently about named highways and interchanges it could not see. safety_overview, risk_level, honest_assessment, checklist and before_you_go are gone, and there is no risk score of any kind. The endpoint takes enum ids (time_of_day, road_type, driver_state, conditions[]), not display labels. limits is ONE server-written string. SECTION RULES, clamped in finalise(): watch_for and prep_checklist are GO-only; safer_options is for pause and do_not_drive only; factors_in_favor is usually [] on anything but a go, because an observation about the driver is not a thing that makes the driving safer. Case 1 is the only case here with a non-empty favor/watch/prep, and that is the point — compare the four against it. driver_state "very_tired" is a SERVER-SIDE boundary: case 4 returns do_not_drive from a localized string table without calling the model, so it must stay byte-stable and must never contain English. Case 3 is the German stress case (four conditions plus a long concern) and guards against truncation. Case 2 is the tool at its best: before_you_decide naming an official road-conditions source and what a closure or a restriction would mean. Case 5 is the grounding case — this exact input produced "Heavy traffic — evening commute conditions", "low-visibility weather", a 20-30 minute recovery prescription, and safer_options inventing a colleague and someone at home. OUTPUT DISCIPLINE and STATE-SPECIFIC OUTPUT RULES were added 2026-08-25 and the sanitiser caps were aligned to them: harder 5, favor 4, safer 4, prep 3, watch 2. A GO answer is now materially SHORTER than a pause — case 1 is ~850 chars against ~1800-2000 for cases 2, 3 and 5. If a future capture shows GO growing back toward the others, the discipline block has stopped working. READ cases 2 and 5 after any prompt change; structure alone will not catch a regression in either. optionalSections on a case names the arrays this tool is DESIGNED to leave empty, so a run that correctly returns [] is not read as a regression; safer_options on a pause and factors_harder on a pause are NOT optional and stay asserted. FATIGUE RULE (owner, 2026-08-25): no short intervention is evidence of readiness — not a brief wait, not the yawning stopping, not food, caffeine, fresh air or a walk. The boundary is actual alertness sustained for the WHOLE drive, and if fatigue remains the answer is not to start. Case 5 is the fatigue case: read its before_you_decide, which should name alertness as the deciding factor and say plainly not to start if it persists. GROUNDING TEST (owner, 2026-08-25): every claim must trace to a user input or be framed as something to CHECK. A selected condition establishes that the driver REPORTED it, not what the road is doing — case 2 should read "You reported snow or ice", never "snow or ice on the road surface", "high wind on exposed highway", "early morning — darkness/temperatures at their lowest", or "your winter-driving skills are rusty". General knowledge may name what to check; it may not be stated as a fact about this drive. Case 2 is the test case for all of it.

input.concern: It is much later than I meant to stay out.

output.headline: Nothing in what you've reported gives a clear reason to wait.
output.summary: You report feeling fine, clear conditions, and a short city-street drive. The only hesitation you noted is the late hour, which is a circumstance rather than an impairment.
factors_harder: Late night — you reported this is later than you intended to be out
factors_in_favor: Short drive — approximately 20 minutes on city streets
prep_checklist: Do a quick self-check before starting: are you alert and able to sustain attention for the full 20 minutes?
watch_for: Late-night city streets can have reduced pedestrian visibility and less predictable traffic — keep attention up at intersections
limits: Drive Home doesn't have live traffic, weather, or road-condition data. This assessment uses only what you reported. If conditions change, reassess before leaving.

input.concern: I have not driven in snow since last winter and I do not know how the pass looks.

output.headline: Check current road and pass conditions before you commit to leaving.
output.summary: You reported snow or ice and high wind on a 90-minute early-morning highway drive, and you have a specific unknown: the pass conditions. That unknown, combined with limited recent snow-driving experience, is enough reason to resolve the facts before starting.
output.main_concern: You reported not knowing how the pass looks, and that is a concrete, checkable fact that materially affects this decision.
factors_harder: You reported snow or ice conditions
Highway drive — limited options to exit or wait once underway
You reported not having driven in snow since last winter
output.before_you_decide: Check the current road conditions and any closure, chain-law, or traction-advisory notices for the pass on your route. A state department of transportation road-conditions site or hotline is the right source — look for the one covering Colorado and Wyoming highways. If the pass is closed, restricted to vehicles you are not equipped for, or carrying an advisory beyond what you feel prepared for, do not start the drive.
safer_options: Wait until current pass and road conditions are confirmed clear and within your comfort level, then reassess
If available, have a driver with recent snow and mountain highway experience make the drive instead
Delay departure until later in the day if conditions are expected to improve — check the forecast and road-conditions updates before deciding on a new window
If the trip can wait, consider travelling on a different day when conditions have cleared
limits: Drive Home doesn't have live traffic, weather, or road-condition data. This assessment uses only what you reported. If conditions change, reassess before leaving.

input.concern: Die Sicht wird schlechter und ich kenne die Umleitung durch die Baustelle nicht.

output.headline: Kurz innehalten – eine konkrete Ungewissheit sollte vor der Abfahrt geklärt werden.
output.summary: Sie berichten Regen, Nebel, starken Verkehr und eine Ihnen unbekannte Umleitung durch eine Baustelle. Die Kombination aus eingeschränkter Sicht und einer unbekannten Streckenführung auf nassen Straßen bei Nacht macht es sinnvoll, die Umleitung vor der Abfahrt zu klären. Sobald Sie die Route kennen, lässt sich die Fahrt besser einschätzen.
output.main_concern: Sie kennen die Umleitung durch die Baustelle nicht.
factors_harder: Regen und Nebel gemeldet – Sie berichten von zunehmend schlechter Sicht
Unbekannte Umleitung: Sie wissen nicht, welcher Weg durch die Baustelle führt
output.before_you_decide: Suchen Sie die Umleitung jetzt, vor der Abfahrt, in einer Navigations-App. Wenn Sie die Route kennen, lässt sich die Fahrt besser einschätzen.
safer_options: Umleitung jetzt am Standort in einer Navigations-App nachschlagen, bevor Sie das Fahrzeug starten
Umleitung jetzt vor der Abfahrt in einer Navigations-App nachschlagen – dann wissen Sie, welcher Weg durch die Baustelle führt.
Abfahrt verschieben, bis Sicht und Verkehr sich verbessern, und Lage dann neu einschätzen
Öffentliche Verkehrsmittel oder ein Taxi/Ridesharing nutzen, falls verfügbar
limits: Drive Home hat keine Live-Daten zu Verkehr, Wetter oder Straßenzustand. Diese Einschätzung verwendet nur das, was du angegeben hast. Wenn sich die Bedingungen ändern, bewerte die Fahrt vor der Abfahrt neu.

output.headline: Fahre jetzt nicht los, wenn du sehr müde bist.
output.summary: Die wichtigste Information ist deine aktuelle Müdigkeit. Verschiebe die Fahrt oder nutze eine andere Möglichkeit, nach Hause zu kommen, statt mit starker Müdigkeit zu fahren.
output.main_concern: Du hast angegeben, sehr müde zu sein.
output.before_you_decide: Bewerte die Fahrt erst neu, wenn du wirklich ausgeruht bist und Wachbleiben und Konzentration kein Problem mehr sind.
safer_options: Warte und ruhe dich aus, bevor du die Fahrt neu bewertest.
Bleib dort, wenn das praktikabel ist.
Bitte eine ausgeruhte Person zu fahren.
Nutze Taxi, Fahrdienst, öffentliche Verkehrsmittel oder eine andere verfügbare Alternative.
limits: Drive Home hat keine Live-Daten zu Verkehr, Wetter oder Straßenzustand. Diese Einschätzung verwendet nur das, was du angegeben hast. Wenn sich die Bedingungen ändern, bewerte die Fahrt vor der Abfahrt neu.

input.concern: I caught myself yawning on the walk to the car and it is raining harder than when I arrived.

output.headline: Wait and reassess your alertness before starting — the yawning before you even reach the car is the key concern.
output.summary: You reported feeling a little tired and caught yourself yawning on the walk out. Before you start a 45-minute drive in rain and heavy traffic, sit for a moment and assess how you actually feel. The key question is whether you feel able to sustain attention for the whole journey.
output.main_concern: Yawning before the drive begins, combined with self-reported tiredness, in conditions that will require sustained attention for 45 minutes.
factors_harder: Yawning noted before even reaching the car
Rain heavier than when you arrived
Heavy traffic reported — conditions that demand consistent attention
output.before_you_decide: Sit in the car without starting it and honestly assess whether you feel able to sustain attention for the full 45 minutes in rain and heavy traffic. If fatigue remains, do not start.
safer_options: Wait at your office until you feel clearly alert, then reassess
Ask someone at your office whether they are heading in your direction, or check whether rideshare or public transit could cover this trip
If available, use a rideshare or public transit for this trip
Consider whether staying where you are until conditions or alertness improve is an option
limits: Drive Home doesn't have live traffic, weather, or road-condition data. This assessment uses only what you reported. If conditions change, reassess before leaving.
